# Willpower @ Stage 12 — Formal Landmark

> developed 2026-07-24.

## Expression on this line

Willpower at Order 11 is formal willpower modeling: the construction of mathematically rigorous
models of self-regulation with provable properties. This is where willpower science becomes
formal: the analyst constructs a formal model (a computational model of self-control, a
dynamical systems model of habit formation, a game-theoretic model of self-regulation) and
proves properties about it (stability, efficiency, complexity bounds).

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** the felt rigor of a formal self-regulation analysis — the researcher who can prove
  their willpower model has the properties it claims.
- **UR:** formal self-regulation models with provable properties.
- **LL:** a scholarly culture of formal self-regulation analysis — the community that evaluates
  willpower models by their formal properties.
- **LR:** the formal frameworks themselves (computational self-control, dynamical systems
  habit models).

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** formalization paralysis — refusing to engage with any self-regulation
  question that cannot be formally modeled.
- **Dark allergy:** formalization absence — making willpower claims that cannot be formally
  articulated or evaluated.
- **Golden addiction:** claiming to compare willpower paradigms (Stage 13) while actually just
  building formal models within a single paradigm.
- **Golden allergy:** refusing to engage with formal willpower models because they seem
  "reductive."

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Formal self-regulation specification:** the willpower model is articulated with internal
  consistency and descriptive precision.
- **Comparative capability:** the framework can be compared with other willpower frameworks on
  shared terms.
- **Formal verification:** the analyst can demonstrate that the self-regulation model achieves
  its stated objectives under specified conditions.

## Sources, joints, open questions

**Sources:** Baumeister & Tierney, *Willpower* (formal self-control science); Wood & Neal,
"A new look at habits and the habit-goal interface" (*Psychological Review*, 2007) (formal
habit modeling).
**Open joints:** How does formal willpower modeling shade into multi-paradigm willpower
coordination (Stage 13)?
**Research debt:** pairs with `11-abstract-emerge` (purpose-driven willpower) and
`13-systematic-green` (multi-paradigm willpower coordination).
